title: OMPTBench - OpenMP Tool Interface Conformance Testing
problem: OpenMP Tool Interface (OMPT) implementation status differs significantly across compilers, making it difficult for tool developers to rely on consistent OMPT support. Many correctness tools and profilers depend on OMPT to obtain runtime event information, but implementation inconsistencies limit their portability and reliability.
motivation: Evaluating and understanding OMPT implementation status across compiler vendors is essential for high-performance computing, where third-party tools and profilers depend on consistent OMPT support.
method: The authors built a conformance test suite—a set of 30 targeted tests that check whether different compilers correctly implement the OpenMP Tool Interface (OMPT), which is the standard way for profiling and debugging tools to observe what parallel programs are doing. The tests examine both the main CPU and GPU events, focusing on specific OMPT features. By running these tests on various compiler versions, particularly AMD's ROCm compiler, they identified which compilers have missing features and tracked their progress toward full compliance.
key_novelty: The key contribution is the first conformance test suite designed to systematically evaluate which compilers properly implement the OpenMP Tool Interface.
contributions: Developed a 30-test-case conformance test suite for evaluating OMPT implementation
Comprehensive coverage of both host-side and device-side OMPT events
Evaluation framework revealing implementation trends across compiler versions
Evidence of AMD ROCm moving toward full device-side OMPT support

metrics.other: test pass rates, OMPT feature coverage across compiler versions

limitations: The test suite is incomplete and provides an initial vehicle for OMPT conformance evaluation rather than comprehensive coverage of all OMPT features and scenarios.
